rubrics.justification: The model explicitly stated that no embryo image was available to it and declined to fabricate morphology. It made no incorrect morphological claims.
It integrated age, ovarian reserve, BMI, tubal factor, sperm parameters, endometrium, and lifestyle well with expected prognosis, though this was necessarily conditional on assumed embryo quality.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability estimates tied to assumed blastocyst quality and favorable patient factors. Minor limitation is reliance on hypothetical morphology.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET in a good-prognosis 31-year-old, morphology-based selection, luteal support, and cautious/optional PGT-A. Mention of ERA/thrombophilia screening is more controversial and less routinely guideline-supported.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, embryo selection, cryopreservation, and contingency planning, though some advice remains generic because morphology was unavailable.
